newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore government securities end narrowly mixed.
newsitem.headline: Singapore government securities end narrowly mixed.

text.p: Singapore government securities ended narrowly mixed on Monday in moderate trade on interbank and retail interest, dealers said.

"Government securities were narrowly mixed today amid uncertainty over the near-term direction of the market. Treasury bill yields were slightly higher but bond prices were narrowly mixed. Volume was moderate," a local dealer said.
In treasury bills, three-months closed at a yield of 1.87/1.82 percent compared with last Friday's yield of 1.78/1.63 percent and one-year at a yield of 1.85/1.80 percent against 1.78/1.63 percent.
Among bonds, April 1999 ended at S$99.50/99.55 from last Friday's close of S$99.53/99.58, September 2001 at S$96.68/96.73 versus S$96.70/96.75 and June 2003 at S$94.75/94.80 against S$94.81/94.86.
The interbank rate was unchanged from last Friday's 3-9/16 3-7/16 percent.
